decisionsTitle: A wide backoffice table has a scrollbar at its top too
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-11-18, with a screenshot of the volunteers' wide list and a box drawn right under its header row:** «mai vreau un UI improvement: vreau sa pot da scroll intr-un tabel si din partea asta de sus, fara sa mai fiu nevoit sa dau scroll pana jos».

**Why it was needed.** A backoffice table wider than its frame scrolls sideways inside that frame (§650), its row verbs pinned to the frame's right edge (§943). The frame's own scrollbar is at its bottom — and on a list of fifty volunteers or registrations the bottom is a page or more away, so reading the columns past the edge meant scrolling down to the end, sideways, and back up.

**Decision.** Every backoffice table that scrolls sideways gets a second horizontal scrollbar right above its frame, kept in step with the frame's own:

- **One small island, `TopScrollbar`** (`src/shared/ui/TopScrollbar.tsx`), drawn by `AdminTable` in one box with its desktop frame. It receives the frame's address — a string, `frameIdFor(tableId)` (`src/shared/ui/top-scrollbar.ts`), the `id` `AdminTable` now puts on its frame — and finds the frame by it; no element crosses the boundary (§370). The table's markup and its server rendering are otherwise unchanged.
- **The frame's one watcher.** The island watches the frame with the chips rows' own `watchScrollRow` (§720 amended), now given the bar as an optional `mirror`. That watcher was already the frame's (it keeps `data-more-end`, which the pinned verbs fade on, §943); it moves from `ColumnWidths` into this island rather than a second one being added, so the scroll, the frame's and the table's sizes and the frame's children are watched once. The bar is shown only while the frame overflows (`scrollWidth > clientWidth + 1`); its one empty child is as wide as the bar plus the frame's room, so both reach exactly as far and one `scrollLeft` is the same column in both; each side writes the other only when they differ by a pixel or more (a zoomed page's fractional positions included), and the «scroll» that echoes its own write answers nothing (`isEcho`: each side remembers the position it was last given, and its next «scroll» at that position is taken as the echo, once) — a browser says «scroll» a frame after the write, when the hand on the other side may already have moved on, and answering that late echo wrote the bar back behind the pointer mid-drag (the review measured it in Chromium: 39 writes to the bar in a 40-step thumb drag, once 23 px back) and would cut a wheel's smooth scroll short; so the side a hand moves is never written; passive listeners.
- **Where it stands.** Sticky at the top of the window under the sticky site header (`HEADER_CLEARANCE_PX.sm`, the clearance every sticky part of the backoffice already uses), inside the box that holds it and the frame — so it stays while its table is on screen and leaves with it — opaque in the colour of what the table stands on (`ADMIN_TABLE_SURFACE`, the page or the card) and above the pinned verbs and the column edges that pass under it.
- **A track one can grab.** Drawn, not left to the platform, since overlay scrollbars (a Mac, a tablet) appear only mid-scroll: 12 px, a thumb in the muted text's colour on the divider's, from `::-webkit-scrollbar` in Chrome and Safari and from `scrollbar-width` / `scrollbar-color` only where that selector is unknown (Firefox) — Chrome drops its `::-webkit-scrollbar` rules once those are set. The palette's variables, both schemes.
- **Decoration, not a control of its own.** `aria-hidden` and `tabIndex={-1}`: the frame stays the keyboard's and the screen reader's, as it was.
- **Server-first.** The server draws it as nothing to see (`display: none` until the island marks it shown), so before hydration and without JavaScript there is no bar and no space kept for one — the frame's own scrollbar at the bottom works as before. Never on the phone's blocks (from `md` up only) and never on paper.
- **The same bar outside `AdminTable`.** The three backoffice tables that scroll sideways on their own frame get it too: the event's emergency sheet (`/admin/events/[id]/urgente`), «Liste date sponsorilor» and the answers of «Răspunsuri „Vin!”» in the event editor. The volunteers' list of the screenshot is an `AdminTable` and has it from there.

**Left out.** A sticky heading row — the column names following the reader down a long list — was not asked and is not built; the size grid of a shop product (a form of inputs) and the design page's reference tables (`/admin/design`, three columns) do not get the bar. The bar is 12 px tall, a pointer's target rather than a thumb's 44 (BR-REQ-041-01 criterion 6): on a touch screen the table itself is what a finger swipes, and the phone's layout has no bar at all.
changelogLine: - **A scrollbar at the top of wide backoffice tables** — a table wider than the screen (the volunteers', the registrations', every list) now has a second horizontal scrollbar right above it, kept in step with the one at its bottom and sticky under the site header while the table is on screen, so it scrolls sideways without going down to its end; also on the emergency sheet, «Liste date sponsorilor» and the «Vin!» answers. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given a backoffice table at `md` and up whose table is wider than its frame — every `AdminTable` list, the event's emergency sheet, «Liste date sponsorilor» and the «Vin!» answers — then right above the frame stands a second horizontal scrollbar reaching exactly as far as the frame's own: scrolling either moves the other to the same place, the one a hand moves never written back (a drag of the bar's thumb never pulls it back under the pointer), and it sticks under the site header while the table is on screen, opaque on the table's surface, a visible track in both schemes, hidden from assistive technology and the keyboard; a table that fits, the phone's blocks, paper, and a page before hydration or without JavaScript show no such bar, the frame's own scrollbar at its bottom working as before (2026-11-18, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
